# Results — Study 208 (Gold-Miners)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). GDX (VanEck Gold Miners ETF)
and GLD (SPDR Gold Shares), daily adjusted closes from Yahoo Finance. Common window from
GDX IPO. As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLD | 2006-05-22 → 2026-06-15 | 5,048 | `355bd4da5568` |
| GDX | 2006-05-22 → 2026-06-15 | 5,048 | `a62e9750e223` |

*Common intersection: **n = 5,047** return observations (one lost to first-difference).*

---

## Test 1 — OLS Beta / Alpha: Is GDX "leveraged gold"?

The recipe regresses daily GDX log-returns on GLD log-returns: `r_GDX = alpha + beta * r_GLD + eps`.
Beta measures how much GDX amplifies gold; alpha captures the annual operational drag vs holding
physical gold. Inference via Newey-West HAC sandwich.

| Parameter | Estimate | HAC *t* | Interpretation |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| **beta (leverage)** | **1.73×** | **+35.35** | Strongly significant — miners *do* amplify gold moves |
| **alpha (drag)** | **−10.6%/yr** | **−2.14** | Significant — mines lose ~10.6% vs gold per year on average |
| R² | 0.58 | — | Gold explains ~58% of daily miner variance |
| GLD vol | 18.3%/yr | — | — |
| GDX vol | 41.3%/yr | — | — |
| Idio vol | 26.7%/yr | — | Large unexplained component (operational, FX, cost risk) |
| Vol-ratio (implied leverage) | 2.26× | — | Raw vol is 2.26× gold — higher than the beta alone |

**The leveraged-gold claim is structurally confirmed**: GDX amplifies gold returns at ~1.73× beta
(HAC *t* = 35.35). However, the operational alpha is **−10.6%/yr** (HAC *t* = −2.14) — statistically
significant drag. Miners are leveraged gold *minus a meaningful, persistent annual fee* payable to
geology, labour, energy, and management.

---

## Test 2 — Asymmetric Beta: More Downside Than Upside?

The popular claim says miners give "more downside than upside" (beta_dn > beta_up). We fit a
dual-slope model with a shared intercept and test the contrast via the Newey-West sandwich.

| Statistic | Value |
|---|--:|
| n_up (gold-up days) | 2,688 |
| n_dn (gold-down days) | 2,359 |
| **beta_up** | **1.84×** |
| **beta_dn** | **1.62×** |
| diff (beta_dn − beta_up) | **−0.22** |
| HAC *t* on diff | **−2.18** |
| asymmetry_ratio (beta_dn / beta_up) | 0.88 |

**The popular claim is rejected — in the wrong direction (|t| = 2.18 against it).** On the
real tape, miners amplify gold-up days *more* (1.84×) than gold-down days (1.62×). The
"leveraged downside" narrative does not survive a symmetric two-sided test on 20 years of data.
This likely reflects the call-option-like payoff of mining stocks: gold prices above the cost
of production give convex upside exposure.

---

## Test 3 — Miners-vs-Bullion Timing Rule

A relative-strength timing rule: hold GDX when the GDX/GLD ratio is above its 200-day SMA,
hold GLD otherwise. The fair comparison is a simple GLD buy-and-hold.

| Strategy | CAGR | Sharpe | Vol | Max DD | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **GLD buy-and-hold** | **+9.4%** | **+0.493** | 18.3%/yr | −45.6% | +2.29 |
| GDX buy-and-hold | +5.1% | +0.120 | 41.3%/yr | −80.6% | +0.57 |
| GDX/GLD timing (5 bps cost) | +3.6% | +0.131 | 27.3%/yr | −52.2% | +0.62 |

*In-market (GDX) fraction: 36.9% of days. Switches: 220 (at 5 bps one-way cost).*

**The timing rule underperforms even simple GLD**: Sharpe 0.131 vs 0.493 for GLD. The rule
rotates into a high-vol, negative-alpha vehicle only 37% of the time and still cannot clear the
GLD hurdle. HAC *t* of 0.62 on timing returns — indistinguishable from zero.

---

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Decisive number |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal** | `WEAK` | Beta=1.73× (t=35.35) is real but well-known; alpha=−10.6%/yr (t=−2.14) dominates economics; asymmetry claim rejected (t=−2.18, opposite direction) |
| **Tradability** | `MIRAGE` | Timing Sharpe 0.131 vs GLD 0.493; GDX CAGR 5.1% vs GLD 9.4%; maxDD −80.6%; timing adds nothing (t=0.62) |
| **Leveraged upside / downside?** | BUSTED | On real tape beta_up=1.84 > beta_dn=1.62 (t=−2.18) — miners have *more* upside convexity, not more downside |

> **In one sentence:** GDX is leveraged gold at ~1.73×, but the ~10.6%/yr operational alpha drain
> (statistically significant) and ~26.7%/yr idiosyncratic volatility mean that over the 2006-2026
> period GLD outperformed GDX by ~4%/yr; the popular "more downside than upside" asymmetry is
> empirically rejected; and a miners-vs-bullion relative-strength timing rule (Sharpe 0.13) falls
> far short of simply holding GLD (Sharpe 0.49).
